added_lemmas.statement: Under the stated recursive semi-Markovian, proxy-intervention, and positive-compatible semantic scope, for every \(A\subseteq V^{-}\), the causal target \(Q_s=Q[\{s\}]=P(s\mid\operatorname{do}(V\setminus\{s\}))\) is identifiable from \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) if and only if the induced graph \(G[V\setminus A]\) contains no member of \(\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\). Equivalently, \(A\cap(F\setminus\{s\})\neq\varnothing\) for every \(F\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\); because \(V\) is finite, this is further equivalent to \(A\cap R\neq\varnothing\) for every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).

source.locator: Definition 1 and Equation (2)/\(\operatorname{ID}_1(S)\), pp. 3--5; Definition 2 and the no-hedge characterization, pp. 5--6; Lemma 3 and its proof, pp. 32--33
source.verbatim_statement: A set \(A\) is a member of \(\operatorname{ID}_1(S)\) if and only if \(A\cap S=\varnothing\) and there is no hedge formed for \(Q[S]\) in \(G_{[V\setminus A]}\).

upstream.citation: Ilya Shpitser and Judea Pearl (2006), ``Identification of Joint Interventional Distributions in Recursive Semi-Markovian Causal Models,'' Proceedings of AAAI, 1219--1226.

proposed_assumptions.condition: The finite graph \(G\) is the observed acyclic directed mixed graph induced by a recursive semi-Markovian structural causal model on observed vertex set \(V\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This supplies the standard causal-model semantics required by the cited identification theorem while leaving the finite graph, hedge, rank, cost, and approximation conditions unchanged.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is semantic scope imported from Akbari--Etesami--Kiyavash and Shpitser--Pearl, not a combinatorial or optimization premise.

proposed_assumptions.condition: For every selected \(A\subseteq V^{-}\), acquisition supplies the proxy interventional law \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This states exactly which experimental distribution is acquired for a chosen intervention set and is the data input of the cited identification equivalence.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is the proxy-experiment observation convention, independent of hedge rank, bow-freeness, costs, vertex orders, and approximation.

proposed_assumptions.condition: Every identifiability claim is interpreted uniformly over positive recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(G\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Akbari--Etesami--Kiyavash define identification using the positive-compatible-model convention; stating it prevents the combinatorial program from silently changing its semantic domain.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is semantic positivity only and supplies no hedge, rank, cost, hardness, or approximation property.

proposed.name: Minimum-cost identifying intervention
proposed.construction: Under the recursive semi-Markovian, proxy-intervention, and positive-compatible semantic scope, an intervention set \(A\subseteq V^{-}\) is feasible exactly when \(Q_s=Q[\{s\}]\) is identifiable from the acquired law \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\). By the hedge-hitting identification lemma, this feasible class is exactly \(\{A\subseteq V^{-}:A\cap R\neq\varnothing\text{ for every }R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\}\). Choose \(A^\star\in\arg\min_{A\subseteq V^{-}}\sum_{v\in A}c(v)\) over this common feasible class; its value is \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former construction defined only a hedge-hitting program. This replacement preserves that combinatorial kernel while explicitly stating, through the cited bridge, that its feasible sets are exactly the proxy interventions identifying the declared causal target.

prose_updates.tldr: Under the standard positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics, acquiring \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) identifies the causal target \(Q_s\) exactly when \(A\) hits every minimal residual hedge. Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion, oriented by a source-vertex order \(\prec\) on \(U\), realizes the edge clutter of every finite simple graph, yielding unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under the promise \(r(G,s)\leq3\), the path classification partitions every minimal residual across target parents and spouses; after polynomial enumeration in the lexicographic order induced by an independently supplied causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), this yields a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm. Consequently, the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum over all positive-rational-cost instances in the promised class with nonempty residual clutter is exactly two; unit-cost complete-graph expansions witness the lower bound, and the Khot--Regev threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\) on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The supplied-order promised enumerator and optimizer-or-rank-violation interface support existing exact solvers without claiming an unrestricted rank-three recognition algorithm.

project_justification.fill: The paper imports the positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian identification bridge: acquisition of \(Q[V\setminus A]\) identifies \(Q_s\) exactly when \(A\) hits every minimal residual hedge. It then proves the four-vertex obstruction classification and exact private-guard representation, transfers objective-preserving hardness, and establishes that the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum is exactly two over all positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise instances with nonempty residual clutter. The private-guard construction uses the source-vertex order \(\prec\) on \(U\). Separately, given a causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), promised enumeration lists residual constraints exactly once in induced lexicographic order before deterministic parent-spouse rounding. Complete-graph gadgets supply the matching sequence, and \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \(2-\epsilon\) hardness holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The certifying optimizer-or-rank-violation interface is provided without asserting unrestricted recognition of the rank promise.

sampling_model.design: The design deterministically selects one proxy intervention set \(A\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\) and acquires \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\). Feasibility means identification of \(Q_s\) from that law under the cited hedge criterion; finite-sample allocation is outside scope.
sampling_model.units: Vertices of the fixed finite observed ADMG \(G\) induced by a recursive semi-Markovian structural causal model.
sampling_model.treatment: Acquisition of the proxy interventional law produced by intervening on the selected vertices \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Identification is interpreted uniformly over positive recursive semi-Markovian models compatible with \(G\), exactly as in the imported convention. This semantic positivity is separate from bow-freeness, hedge rank, costs, approximation, and vertex orders.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl provide the underlying complete hedge obstruction for recursive semi-Markovian models. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash define positive-compatible-model identification, reduce a single proxy acquisition \(Q[V\setminus A]\) to the no-hedge condition in \(G[V\setminus A]\), and formulate minimum-cost intervention design as minimum-weight hedge hitting. They prove unrestricted hardness and settle bounded residual size through two; their boundary is continued here at the first nonzero finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow an immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the argument, while the parent-spouse threshold proof here acts directly on weighted causal residuals and yields the factor-two upper bound over the full positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise class after exact-once enumeration using the supplied causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\). This enumerator order is independent of the source-vertex order \(\prec\) used to orient private-guard expansions. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred to the narrower unit-cost radius-two-bidirected-tree subclass by the exact private-guard realization. Singh's LP-gap formula motivates the complete-graph sequence witnessing the matching supremum, but no sharpening of that source result is claimed. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine; neither that routine nor the supplied-order promised enumerator is presented as unrestricted rank-three recognition.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The equivalence between identification of \(Q_s\) from the acquired proxy law \(Q[V\setminus A]\) and hitting every minimal residual hedge is imported under the positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian convention; no finite-sample estimation or weaker-positivity extension is claimed. The exact weighted integrality-gap supremum ranges over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty residual clutter. Its matching sequence and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional approximation lower bound use the narrower unit-cost private-guard subclass whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree. Source complexity theorems and rational LP solution are imported. Private-guard construction takes a source-vertex order \(\prec\) on \(U\), whereas the promised algorithms take a distinct causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), used only to make residual output lexicographic and exact once. The complexity of recognizing rank at most three, planar bounded-degree causal realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open. Weighted \(O(3^k)\) exact search is asserted only for a supplied cardinality bound.
